name: WishlistGenius – Wishlist for WooCommerce
author: Plugins.shop

sections.description:
WishlistGenius adds a free wishlist to WooCommerce. Shoppers can save favorite products and return when ready to buy. Guests can save without an account.

Live demos | Manual | Free vs Pro | Support

Included in Free

  • Save products: one wishlist per guest or account, without a fixed product-count ceiling. Save simple products or a chosen size/colour variation.
  • Organize favorites: private notes, search, sorting, manual ordering and grid/list views.
  • Share or export: share by link without exposing notes/account details; export CSV or print through the browser, including Save as PDF.
  • Return to the cart: add an individual saved product, then adjust quantities in the WooCommerce cart.
  • Fit your store: blocks/shortcodes, an Elementor widget, labels, icons, colours and header/mobile access.
  • Manage locally: aggregate totals and privacy export/erasure tools. No payment, publisher account or trial deadline; reporting/newsletter signup is optional.

Optional Pro add-on

The separate paid add-on provides multiple wishlists, saved quantities, selected/all-item cart actions, cart save-for-later, imports, quotes and public discovery. It also adds individual wishlist inspection, product-demand reports and permission-based back-in-stock/price-drop alerts, reminders and campaigns.

Pro requires licence activation. Email needs configuration and customer permission; saving never subscribes anyone. Free’s hideable fictional Pro previews enable no paid tools or sending.

Related plugins by Plugins.shop

Optional, separate tools; none is required or automatically integrated:

  • CatalogFAQ — Publish reusable product FAQs.
  • Cartdini — Ask checkout questions and save answers with the order.
  • Frictions — Investigate checkout issues with protected session replay.

Privacy

Wishlist data stays in your WordPress database: products/variations, quantities, notes, lists/sharing, guest/account IDs, activity, cart records and purchase attribution. Management requires WooCommerce permissions. Sharing excludes notes/account details; Pro discovery follows the store’s directory setting.

The signed wgg_guest cookie defaults to 30 days (1–365 configurable). Shorter retention caps existing database expiry; access stops then even if the cookie lasts longer. Cron deletes expired guests. Activity/jobs default to 90 days, cart records one day; account lists stay until deleted. Orders follow store policy.

Privacy tools cover account data, purchase attribution and retained Pro data. Failed erasure remains incomplete for retry. Pending purchase-suppression retries defer account notifications; a total storage outage can prevent retry storage.

Full retention, admin/browser preferences, local collection/review controls and cart recovery details: bundled privacy-and-controls.txt. Explain your store’s retention and mail providers in its privacy policy.

Optional external service

Setup offers two independent, unchecked, skippable choices after the storefront save. Change them in Privacy & email preferences. They do not authorize shopper mail, Pro licensing or publisher update checks.

Service endpoint | Privacy policy | Service terms

  • Installation sharing: hostname, reported edition, plugin/WordPress/PHP versions and language, at most weekly via cron. No URL paths/queries, shopper records or orders. Address changes pause reporting pending review; reports do not prove ownership or count all installations.
  • Email signup: entered email and reported edition for tips, releases, articles and occasional Pro offers. A prefilled admin email is sent only on selecting/saving this choice; email-only signup sends no hostname. New signups need inbox confirmation and start with all topics/weekly articles. Existing preferences remain; change topics or unsubscribe by email link. Purchase-history personalization/link tracking need separate choices. Edition does not prove purchase.
  • Security: random connection ID, protected credential and consent version accompany requests. The service records consent/report times and receives the network address for security logs. No shopper data, orders, names, wishlist contents, plugin lists or workflow counts are sent.
  • Withdrawal: local reporting stops before remote withdrawal; failures are retryable. Stopping email/edition sharing cancels pending signup for that connection. Confirmed subscriptions need the email’s preferences/unsubscribe link. Skipping creates no connection; deactivation stops reporting, not confirmed subscriptions.
  • Retention: reports/connections expire after 90 days without refresh; pseudonymous revocation records may remain that long. Pending emails expire after 48 hours; confirmed records within 730 days unless explicitly renewed. Consent/suppression history lasts 180 days. Cleanup/outages/backups affect deletion. Acceptance does not prove delivery/subscription.

WordPress export/erasure covers local choices for the supplied admin email. Stop domain-only connections in Privacy & email preferences.
sections.installation:
Requires single-site WordPress 6.7+, WooCommerce 10.0+, PHP 8.2+ and JavaScript. Multisite is unsupported. Wishlist-to-cart requires MySQL/MariaDB with working named locks; SQLite-based WordPress Playground can demonstrate saving but its cart locking is unsupported.

On WordPress 6.7, use a WooCommerce version that supports it, such as 10.3.8. Newer WooCommerce releases may require newer WordPress.

  1. Activate WooCommerce, then WishlistGenius. Individual activation opens Setup & settings.
  2. Choose a wishlist page and button placement, then Save and continue. Both reporting/email choices are optional.
  3. Use Try your wishlist to save a published product, view the list and test adding it to the cart. Exit focus returns to WordPress.

Reopen from WishlistGenius. Bulk/CLI activation and updates do not redirect. Test placement on staging.

Update Free first, then matching Pro 0.5.8, by replacing files without uninstalling. Data remains stored. Older Pro 0.3.x/0.4.x is incompatible; unfinished old batches are not replayed. Check the cart before retrying. Activate Pro in Licence & updates.
sections.faq:
How long does a guest wishlist last?

A signed cookie reconnects the browser. The default is 30 days, configurable to 1–365. Shorter settings also shorten existing guest retention; see Privacy below.

Can customers share a private wish list?

Yes. Lists start private. Share by link, then make private or replace the link to revoke access. Notes and account details stay private.

How do I add a wishlist button, page or counter?

Use blocks, the Elementor widget or [wishlist_genius], [wishlist_genius_button product_id="123"] and [wishlist_genius_counter]. Replace 123 with the product ID; test placement with your theme.

Are variable products and product add-ons supported?

Free supports selected variations. Bundles, bookings, subscriptions and product add-ons need adapters and testing. WooCommerce native wishlists remain separate.

Does Free include cart save-for-later or customer emails?

Free saves products to a wishlist and adds them to the cart individually. Cart save-for-later, saved quantities, batch cart actions and customer emails require Pro. Free shows aggregate totals; individual wishlist inspection and product-demand reports are Pro. Inspection excludes private notes and shopper identities.

What happens when I uninstall?

Data stays by default, including when removing Pro. To delete plugin data/settings, previews, generated coupons, scheduled work and local licence credentials, set WG_DELETE_DATA_ON_UNINSTALL to boolean true before uninstalling Free. Orders, products and pages remain. Release a Pro site slot first in Licence & updates > Advanced: staging and connection management > Release this site.

Are there limits for large wishlists?

There is no fixed saved-product ceiling. Hosting capacity, short rate limits and concurrent cart safeguards still apply. Search/export/print read the complete list in pages; changing a list during export stops it with an error. See bundled privacy-and-controls.txt for cart receipt retention and recovery.

If the host temporarily limits requests, wait for the retry countdown before trying again. Requests that stall show an error; the plugin does not automatically retry cart writes. Check the WooCommerce cart after an uncertain result. Persistent HTTP 429 responses require your host to inspect its request limits.
sections.changelog:
0.5.8

  • Support WordPress 6.7 and newer while retaining the PHP 8.2 minimum.
  • Keep existing wishlist, cart, privacy and security behavior unchanged.
  • Refresh native Free and Pro screenshots, static examples and screenshot descriptions with fictional store data.

0.5.7

  • Share session reads between header counts, save buttons and the wishlist to reduce overlapping requests.
  • Bound stalled requests, respect host retry delays and provide explicit wishlist recovery without automatically repeating cart writes.
  • Distinguish an unavailable database cart lock from temporary contention and refresh Pro copy/move counters.

0.5.6

  • Show saved buttons with a filled icon, clear saved label and matching accessible state; refresh membership when returning to the page.
  • Clearly label search counts as matching saved selections.
  • Preserve private-note and other PATCH update bodies using WordPress method override, including in WordPress Playground; retain version and ownership checks.

0.5.5

  • Stop failed personal-data erasure with a WordPress error so it cannot skip a failed page or mark the request complete.
  • Isolate purchase-suppression failures from WooCommerce order-status changes and retry persisted work during retention cleanup.
  • Apply shorter guest retention to existing wishlists atomically with the settings save and use current settings for new guests.

Older changes and upgrade notices are in bundled changelog.txt.
